-# (Cron version -- $Id: crontab.c,v 2.13 1994/01/17 03:20:37 vixie Exp $)
+#
+# cron-consolidation-phase6 (2026-07-29): every real job from
+# CRONTAB_BACKUP_BEFORE_OOM_PAUSE_2026-07-26.txt has been migrated to a
+# systemd --user timer/service pair (see
+# /opt/veridian/ai-os/stage_c_review_2026-07-29_NOT_INSTALLED/*.timer,*.service
+# for the reviewed, not-yet-installed unit files, and MANIFEST.txt for the
+# full old-job -> new-unit mapping). Root cause this migration fixes: this
+# crontab's own minute-0-aligned schedule with zero jitter and zero shared
+# concurrency cap was the real trigger of the 2026-07-26 OOM-kill/800% CPU
+# incident. systemd timers give this box 3 things cron cannot:
+#   1. RandomizedDelaySec -- real per-activation jitter, not just a fixed
+#      offset, so repeated runs never re-align even over long uptimes.
+#   2. ConditionPathExists=!.../resource-governor-EMERGENCY_STOP on every
+#      single new unit -- a job flagged by resource_governor.py's own
+#      always-on tick loop (veridian-governor-tick.service) now refuses to
+#      even start, not just voluntarily check a flag after starting.
+#   3. Independent per-job start/stop/log accounting via `systemctl --user
+#      status veridian-cron-<name>`, instead of one shared cron log stream.
+#
+# This file is intentionally left with NO active job lines. Activation of
+# the new systemd timers (systemctl --user enable --now ...) is a separate,
+# deliberate cutover step, explicitly NOT done as part of authoring this
+# file -- see this task's own Stage D note. Until that step happens, NO
+# scheduled job of any kind is running on this box (matches the current
+# #STOPPED-ALL-CRON-2026-07-26# state exactly -- this migration does not
+# change that).
